original_question: Determine whether the cardinality of a minimal presentation of a symmetric numerical semigroup can be bounded solely as a function of the embedding dimension.
target_in_paper: Section 5, 'Presentations of a numerical semigroup': "However, the problem of determining if the cardinality of a minimal presentation of a symmetric numerical semigroup can be bounded in function of the embedding dimension remains open."
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact unresolved issue stated in the paper: it concerns symmetric numerical semigroups, the cardinality of a minimal presentation, and whether that quantity is bounded using only the embedding dimension. It is narrowly scoped and does not drift into the broader false conjecture mentioned just before the open problem.
missing_details: The quantifiers should be made explicit: the question is whether there exists a function f: N -> N such that, for every symmetric numerical semigroup S, the cardinality of a minimal presentation of S is at most f(e(S)).
The ambient object should be stated: S is a numerical semigroup, i.e. a subset S of N that contains 0, is closed under addition, and has finite complement in N.
The symmetry hypothesis should be defined: if F(S) denotes the Frobenius number of S, then S is symmetric when x not in S implies F(S) - x in S for every integer x.
The embedding dimension should be identified as e(S), the cardinality of the unique minimal system of generators of S.

The bounded invariant should be defined precisely: a minimal presentation is a finite relation set sigma subseteq N^{e(S)} x N^{e(S)} such that S is isomorphic to N^{e(S)}/<sigma> and |sigma| is as small as possible.
To stay paper-faithful, the question should ask only for existence of some bound depending on e(S), not for the stronger explicit bound recorded just before and then refuted by Barucci.
No further hypotheses such as fixed multiplicity, fixed Frobenius number, complete intersection, or fixed embedding dimension are part of the paper's open problem.
refined_question: Let S be a numerical semigroup, i.e. S is a subset of N containing 0, closed under addition, and with finite complement in N. Let F(S) be its Frobenius number, and assume that S is symmetric, meaning that for every integer x, if x is not in S then F(S) - x is in S. Let e(S) denote the embedding dimension of S, namely the cardinality of its unique minimal system of generators. If sigma is a minimal presentation of S, in the sense that sigma is a finite subset of N^{e(S)} x N^{e(S)} with S isomorphic to N^{e(S)}/<sigma> and |sigma| minimal among all such presentations, does there exist a function f: N -> N such that |sigma| <= f(e(S)) for every symmetric numerical semigroup S?
justification: The draft is aimed at the final open problem in Section 5, not at the stronger conjectured explicit bound cited from [36]. Section 5 first defines presentations and minimal presentations for numerical semigroups, then recalls that arbitrary numerical semigroups do not admit an embedding-dimension-only upper bound on the size of a minimal presentation, and that the symmetric embedding-dimension-4 case is very restricted. After noting that Barucci disproved the stronger conjecture, the paper isolates the surviving problem exactly as whether some bound depending only on embedding dimension exists for symmetric numerical semigroups. To make the question fully stand-alone, one must unpack 'bounded solely as a function of the embedding dimension' into an existence statement for a universal function f, and define numerical semigroup, symmetric, embedding dimension, and minimal presentation.
